items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I mean Debussy and Ravel and all those guys, they broke the rules of the guys before them

ctx.x: enharmonic scale” or something. And I don’t use them, so I’m sometimes stumped as to what to say to that person.

Well I always tell them to look at the notes that are involved. I mean the notes themselves will give you the answers. And when it comes down initially to how does it sound, because the ear is the final judge of that. And you may go by the rules all the time but I mean a lot of rules have been broken because this sounds a certain way and if it sounds right then it’s right. And if that’s the way you want to go nobody can dispute that from you, you say well that’s what I meant to do, that’s the way I wanted to go.…

particular time. And once it’s out you say well there it is. And if you record it there it is. We can’t — “well let’s do it again.” You can do that in the recording studio but if you’re playing a live performance you can’t. I told a kid that — “wait minute, stop the band, I didn’t mean to play that, start again.” You’re in a night club. You can’t do that.
